pages.title: Accounts, character creation and vocation selection
pages.summary: Every new character selects one permanent FactionId, one permanent CombatDisciplineId (combat class), and one changeable primary VocationId. These identities are independent; every available combat discipline supports every available vocation. Character creation is an atomic durable operation, not the act of spawning a Pawn.

sections.title: Player mechanic and scope

These identities are independent; every available combat discipline supports every available vocation. Character creation is an atomic durable operation, not the act of spawning a Pawn.
Committed requirement: one-human core progression remains available. Recommended initial choices below are design work, not compiled engine behavior.

sections.title: Definition, runtime, durable state and view

rows: UAppearanceCatalog, UCombatDisciplineDefinition and UVocationDefinition resolve permitted stable IDs through DA_GameCatalog. FactionId must resolve through the approved faction specification, independently of class/vocation and reputation. AccountPolicy retains character-slot and name rules; definitions hold no player inventory or credentials.
ABriarwakeGameMode admits a verified character-session lease. ABriarwakePlayerController routes owned commands. A newly spawned ABriarwakeCharacter is only the current body.

The persistence boundary writes Record_Account, Record_Character and Record_CommandReceipt atomically with the normalized name reservation and unique starter kit. Record_Character owns permanent FactionId/CombatDisciplineId, active VocationId and independent Progression.Combat / Progression.Vocations histories; its Revision versions the complete progression/build projection.

WBP_Login → WBP_CharacterSelect → WBP_CharacterCreate → WBP_HUD. Publish only the permitted public identity/appearance subset. UCharacterStateComponent exposes owner-only committed progression, including inactive vocation histories; raw records, account identity and authentication tokens are never public PlayerState fields.

sections.title: Editor and configuration recipe
steps: Create the three widgets under Content/Game/UI/Frontend. Keep appearance, faction, combat discipline and vocation selections separate. Focus order: name, appearance, faction, combat discipline, vocation, confirm, back. Explain the permanent faction/class choices before confirmation; UI validation does not replace server validation.

Assign available discipline/vocation definitions and the allowed appearance catalog in DA_GameCatalog; connect the approved faction selection catalog without class/vocation filters. Keep Woodwright and Apothecary unavailable before their existing Phase 20/21 activation. Required choices cannot be omitted because a definition is unavailable.

Configure the server map separately from the client frontend. Phase 05 uses disposable identity fixtures; Phase 06 exercises durable transactions with isolated fixtures. Real character creation stays blocked until the approved faction catalog and Phase 12 discipline definitions are integrated. Do not silently choose a class or retain disposable fixtures as player characters.

sections.title: Native ownership and Blueprint boundary
paragraphs: All Briarwake class and command names are proposed custom project APIs. They are not installed Blueprint nodes. C++ validates durable/gameplay invariants; Blueprint configures reviewed content and presentation.
ABriarwakeGameMode admits a verified character-session lease. ABriarwakePlayerController routes owned commands. A newly spawned ABriarwakeCharacter is only the current body.

Reject an invalid or expired lease, an unknown content ID, a stale revision, insufficient capacity or permission before mutating state. Return a stable error code and refresh the current projection; do not ask the player to repeat an unknown-outcome transaction with a new request ID.

sections.title: Wire the actual player flow
steps: Submit CreateCharacter(RequestId, Name, AppearanceIds, FactionId, CombatDisciplineId, VocationId) from the authenticated account context. The service derives AccountId; it is not trusted from the form. Include every semantic selection in the existing request digest.
Normalize the name with a pinned Unicode policy, validate length and forbidden characters, then acquire account-slot and name constraints in one transaction.

After independent catalog/availability checks, atomically create CharacterId, permanent FactionId/CombatDisciplineId, active VocationId, initial Progression.Combat and exactly one keyed Progression.Vocations entry. Initialize validated Level-1 XP, name reservation, safe starting position and the unique starter-kit outcome/receipt together. A matching request returns the original CharacterId, not another kit.
Reserve a session lease before admitting the body. Bind the local view to the admitted CharacterId and pull its snapshot.

Reconnect from another client after logging out. Display the same permanent faction/class, active vocation, saved vocation histories and appearance without granting another kit or replaying progression rewards.

sections.title: Configured route fixture
paragraphs: Account fixture acct-bw-001 has two permitted slots; char-bw-hearth uses discipline.vanguard and vocation.hearthkeeper at zone.thornmere / spawn.square. Resolve FactionId from the approved faction fixture; no real faction ID is authored on the audited main baseline. Slot counts and locations remain test values, not a replacement faction starting-region policy.
Use L_ThornmereVillage and L_ElderwoodRoad as the repeated route. The isolated L_BriarwakePreview exists only to prove imported visuals. Field values below are fixtures, not production balance.

rows: Create the Vanguard/Hearthkeeper with an approved faction, enter Thornmere, log out, restart and reconnect. Permanent identities, independent progression and all vocation records persist; one character, one starter kit and one active lease exist. See Fixture_identity for trainer-switch and migration acceptance.
Race two requests for the same normalized name, then race two logins for the same character. Exactly one name reservation and one current lease win; the losing session cannot spend inventory.
At 30 simulated admissions measure name-constraint conflicts, admission latency and lease cleanup. These are future connected-client tests, not results from this package.

sections.title: Rejected commands, disconnect and restart
paragraphs: Missing combat discipline → CombatDisciplineRequired; unsupported/unavailable discipline → CombatDisciplineUnavailable. Missing vocation → VocationRequired; unsupported/unavailable vocation → VocationUnavailable. Missing/invalid faction → FactionRequired/FactionUnavailable; absent approved catalog → IdentityCatalogUnavailable. Unsupported cosmetic → AppearanceUnavailable; full slots → CharacterLimit; duplicate normalized name → NameUnavailable. Reject before any name/item/identity mutation.

Persist the operation receipt in the same transaction as its effects. On a lost response, query or retry the same request identity. A successful receipt returns the original result; a changed payload under that identity is rejected. A UI timeout is not proof of a database rollback.

sections.title: UI, animation and accessibility
paragraphs: WBP_Login → WBP_CharacterSelect → WBP_CharacterCreate → WBP_HUD. Publish only the permitted public identity/appearance subset. UCharacterStateComponent exposes owner-only committed progression, including inactive vocation histories; raw records, account identity and authentication tokens are never public PlayerState fields.

Bind observers, pull the current snapshot, and unbind on teardown. Preserve controller focus, localized error text and an accessible alternative to timing-only or sound-only cues. A widget’s disappearance is not a gameplay commit.

sections.title: Art, maturity and stop condition
paragraphs: No archive was available. The character preview must use explicitly audited combinations before it can be accepted; do not infer skins from vocation names.
Authentication-provider selection, password recovery implementation and jurisdiction-specific retention policy remain unresolved. Do not build an ad hoc password store in Unreal.

sections.title: Required selections and permanent identity guards
paragraphs: Committed requirement: faction, combat class (the existing combat discipline) and vocation are three independent identities. Appearance remains a separate cosmetic choice. Validate each selection against its own approved available definitions; do not create faction/class/vocation combination restrictions.

After successful creation, every durable mutation compares permanent FactionId and CombatDisciplineId with the stored values. A client-supplied replacement, generic record patch or unauthorized server-side mutation returns PermanentIdentityLocked before any write. No class-change operation, token, alternate active class or multiclass record is permitted. Controlled legacy completion below is not a gameplay class-change API.

Creation reserves the name and account slot, writes the complete identities and initial progression, grants the starter kit under the existing domain uniqueness guard, and commits the original-result receipt/outbox in one transaction. Reject malformed/missing/unavailable fields before reserving anything. A different payload under the same RequestId returns RequestIdentityConflict. No Pawn or UI can finalize partial creation.

rows: Exactly one approved, available permanent allegiance; independent of reputation, class and vocation
Exactly one available UCombatDisciplineDefinition.DefinitionId; permanent after creation
Exactly one available UVocationDefinition.VocationId; initialize its keyed history once

sections.title: Content readiness without roadmap reordering
paragraphs: The audited main contains generic faction reputation prose but no approved permanent-allegiance catalog/creation specification. Supply that existing faction work as a compatibility prerequisite; this change does not invent faction IDs, starting regions or lore. An absent catalog returns IdentityCatalogUnavailable; never default allegiance or drop the required field.

Phase 05 retains disposable selection fixtures and Phase 06 isolated persistence tests. UCombatDisciplineDefinition and its four data assets still activate at Phase 12 (ADR-004); re-open character creation then with approved faction content. Earlier fixture success is not production admission readiness. Real characters cannot be created until every required selected definition is integrated and available.

pages.title: Eight-way movement, hop, swimming and input
pages.summary: Movement is on a flat X/Y gameplay plane. Eight input sectors are supported, but only four sprite facings are promised initially. Sprint, dodge, a bounded low-obstacle hop and authored-water swimming are distinct server-validated action states; there is no climbing.

sections.title: Definition, runtime, durable state and view

rows: UMovementProfile stores speeds, stamina costs, hop distance/duration, eligible obstacle tags and water-entry rules. UZoneDefinition identifies walkable cells, low obstacles, water and exits.

UBriarwakeMovementComponent controls collision and movement. The autonomous client may predict movement after the movement integration is verified; the server rejects impossible paths. UActionExecutionComponent arbitrates exclusive actions.
Record_Character saves safe zone/checkpoint and committed transition state. Do not persist every animation frame or treat a client position as a durable checkpoint.

Input Action IA_Move supplies a normalized Vector2D. UCharacterAppearanceComponent projects velocity or aim onto four available facings. WBP_HUD shows stamina and water/hop restrictions without calculating authority.

sections.title: Editor and configuration recipe
steps: Use a Paper2D map transformed into the X/Y plane and a non-rendered collision floor compatible with CharacterMovement. Keep the capsule upright. Orient the sprite plane toward the fixed orthographic camera; do not rotate the camera at runtime.
Create IMC_Gameplay with keyboard and controller bindings. Normalize diagonals before mapping to world axes. Disable orient-to-movement rotation for the visual root; select sprite facing instead.

Mark one low fence as hop-eligible and one deep pool as swim-eligible in the Thornmere fixture. Give both explicit exit cells; a water texture alone cannot authorize swimming. Exact custom movement-mode integration is an engine verification gate.

sections.title: Wire the actual player flow
steps: IA_Move → owning controller → character movement input; UI focus may suppress local gameplay input but never pauses the server.
The server checks action state, speed budget, collision and legal water transitions. Hop requests include a candidate direction, never an authoritative landing point.
Sweep the proposed hop corridor and landing footprint; reject unmarked walls, occupied landings and wrong water states. Reserve or revalidate a landing to resolve simultaneous hops.
Advance the authoritative action window and collision policy. Cosmetic sprite lift must not move the authoritative capsule or change hit range.
Replicate action state and facing. Restore normal movement only after a valid landing or a server-selected recovery cell.

sections.title: Configured route fixture
paragraphs: In L_ThornmereVillage place a 32-unit test tile grid, fence.low.01, wall.solid.01 and water.safe.01. Use 160 units/s walk and 240 sprint solely as tuning examples.
Use L_ThornmereVillage and L_ElderwoodRoad as the repeated route. The isolated L_BriarwakePreview exists only to prove imported visuals. Field values below are fixtures, not production balance.

rows: Walk cardinally and diagonally for an equal interval, hop the low fence but not the solid wall, enter and leave eligible water, and recover after an interrupted dodge.
Two clients observe identical facing/action states. Race for a hop landing and reject a spoofed distant landing; neither body is allowed into a blocked cell.
At 1/2/5/10/30 clients record correction frequency, movement bandwidth and crowded-door recovery, including packet loss and delayed input.

paragraphs: Out-of-range hop → InvalidLanding. Swim outside eligible water → WaterRequired. Dodge during committed crafting → ActionBusy. Disconnection cancels uncommitted actions and retains the last safe recoverable position.

steps: Receive server-approved appearance IDs, action type, facing and action start time.

Play cosmetic notifications only. Stopping playback, suppressing notifies or hiding the character cannot change authoritative rewards.

pages.title: Combat, GAS, disciplines and talents
pages.summary: Combat combines server-resolved melee and projectiles with optional soft targeting for abilities and healing. Vanguard, Ranger, Arcanist and Warden are independent of the five vocations. Every discipline must have a viable solo path.

sections.title: Definition, runtime, durable state and view

rows: UCombatDisciplineDefinition, UTalentDefinition and authored GameplayAbility/GameplayEffect classes define available actions, costs, cooldowns and branch prerequisites. Tuning is authored data, not widget logic.

The PlayerState-associated AbilitySystemComponent and UCombatAttributeSet own runtime ability/attribute behavior. ABriarwakeCharacter is the current avatar. Server traces and target validation decide hits; PaperZD observes action state.

Record_Character.CombatDisciplineId is permanent after creation. Progression.Combat stores independent TotalXP, DefinitionVersion, PurchasedTalentIds and UnspentTalentPoints. Record_Character.Revision is also the progression/build revision; derive level and rebuild abilities from validated definitions without replaying rewards. Vocation changes preserve this entire combat record and its grants; talent respec remains within the chosen discipline.
WBP_HUD displays health/stamina/mana, cooldowns and action errors; WBP_Talents requests purchases. Keyboard and controller can select the same valid targets.

Place BP_TrainingDummy on the connected Elderwood route. Start with one trace shape and one projectile; disable visual damage notifies to prove rules remain server-driven.

sections.title: Wire the actual player flow
steps: Ability input requests activation through the owning controller/ability component. Server checks lease, state, resource cost, cooldown, target and current committed grant permission. Commit permitted runtime cost once and open the authored hit window. The server chooses collision results and line-of-sight eligibility.
Apply damage/healing through the selected GAS effects. Track legitimate support and damage participation for rewards.
On a durable reward, request the persistence transaction using encounter/reward identity; do not award XP in the damage widget.
Rebuild talents/equipment-derived grants after respawn or transfer; remove old handles before reapplying the new avatar binding.

pages.summary: Enemies patrol authored routes, detect eligible targets, leash to safe encounter bounds and reset under explicit rules. Death is a server state transition. Reward eligibility includes declared healing/support contribution and must not depend on the last hit.

paragraphs: Use the existing ANpcServiceActor/UNpcServiceDefinition trainer interaction and eligibility checks for ChangeVocation; no new NPC hierarchy or service is needed. The authoritative identity operation preserves quest/faction/region state while changing only the active vocation and its permitted initial record/debit.

paragraphs: All Briarwake class and command names are proposed custom project APIs. They are not installed Blueprint nodes. C++ validates durable/gameplay invariants; Blueprint configures reviewed content and presentation.
Dedicated zones validate gameplay commands and use server-only credentials. The persistence boundary applies lease fencing, transactions, authorization and audit controls.

Reject an invalid or expired lease, an unknown content ID, a stale revision, insufficient capacity or permission before mutating state. Return a stable error code and refresh the current projection; do not ask the player to repeat an unknown-outcome transaction with a new request ID.

sections.title: Wire the actual player flow
steps: Deploy matched server/client/content/schema versions into a nonproduction environment.
Admit an authenticated character through an active lease; rate-limit and validate every value-changing command.
Inject zone crash, response loss, database timeout and duplicate request at named transaction boundaries.
Restore a backup into an isolated environment, reconcile receipts/outbox and validate that the restored world has one canonical state.
Publish measured results with environment and raw evidence. Mark unsupported platform/provider/version cases Not run rather than passing them by assumption.

sections.title: Rejected commands, disconnect and restart
paragraphs: Fail closed on invalid identity or fencing token. A storage outage rejects new durable mutations or keeps a precisely recorded pending state; it does not silently fall back to local SaveGame truth.

Persist the operation receipt in the same transaction as its effects. On a lost response, query or retry the same request identity. A successful receipt returns the original result; a changed payload under that identity is rejected. A UI timeout is not proof of a database rollback.

sections.title: UI, animation and accessibility
paragraphs: Operational dashboards show aggregate latency, errors, contention, replication, crashes and progression stalls. Player-facing UI shows maintenance and recovery states without leaking internal credentials.

Bind observers, pull the current snapshot, and unbind on teardown. Preserve controller focus, localized error text and an accessible alternative to timing-only or sound-only cues. A widget’s disappearance is not a gameplay commit.

pages.title: Briarwake · game overview
pages.summary: An entirely 2D persistent-world action RPG whose essential PvE progression remains available to one human.

sections.title: The player promise
paragraphs: Committed requirement: combat, exploration, dynamic chosen professions, world development and social play are comparable pillars. A quiet server must still support the complete required PvE adventure, vocation mastery and critical regional improvements. More people add cooperation, variety and recognition rather than mandatory dependencies.

sections.title: What the game is
paragraphs: Briarwake uses a fixed three-quarter top-down pixel-art presentation, X/Y movement input, authored 2D tile layers and loading transitions between bounded zones. Initial facing art is four-direction; eight-way movement does not imply eight-direction sprites. Sprint, dodge, a short eligible-obstacle hop and swimming are committed. Climbing, platformer precision traversal, 3D terrain and camera rotation are not.

sections.title: Two independent identities
paragraphs: Each playable character must choose exactly one primary vocation: Forgekeeper, Hearthkeeper, Wayfinder, Woodwright or Apothecary. All characters can fight, explore, harvest basic materials and use baseline NPC services. Vanguard, Ranger, Arcanist and Warden describe proposed combat disciplines, not replacements for vocation choice.

sections.title: The recurring route
paragraphs: Begin in Thornmere village, meet a mentor, choose an outing along Elderwood Road, encounter a threat or use a calmer investigation route, obtain and transform useful materials, and contribute to the North Road repair. Returning players see the committed bridge/watchtower state and newly available services. That same route receives the features in Phases 00–31.

sections.title: What exists in this delivery
paragraphs: An offline documentation site, source registries, source-preserving requirement coverage, deterministic generators, validators and arithmetic/design tests. No Unreal game project, runtime C++ implementation, sprite pack, third-party plugin, server binary or database has been generated. The full master-prompt acceptance contract is not yet satisfied.

sections.title: Explicitly deferred
paragraphs: PvP, conquest, taxation, player political governance, player housing, auction houses, unrestricted terrain modification, endless procedural worlds and massive mandatory raids are not part of the committed baseline. Scaling beyond the initial 1–30 test population requires measurements.

pages.title: Vision and balanced pillars
pages.summary: Design each feature to connect at least two pillars without forcing every player into every activity.

rows: Readable action challenges, gear choices and combat talents
Salvage/defense supplies profession and region objectives.
Permanent authored stages and useful services
Different vocation products, clues and encounters advance shared projects.
Clues, paths, discoveries and original places
Useful sites, ingredients, lore and threat information support other activities.
Meaningful material/technique choices in short varied loops
Equipment, food, remedies and supports change outing preparation and world results.
Parties, trade and guild projects enrich existing access rather than gate it.

sections.title: Avoid compulsory chores
paragraphs: No mandatory daily attendance, punitive offline crop decay, idle helper farming, player-only essential service, vocation-only critical quest ingredient or population quota may block the main route. A calm session may still include decisions and movement; combat is not required in every single five-minute activity.

sections.title: What changes and what does not
paragraphs: A permanent bridge changes traversal and services. Regional danger can renew through explicitly authored events. Personal discovery remains individually meaningful after shared progress. Do not implement unbounded terrain simulation or erase major improvements to force repetition.

sections.title: Quality measures
paragraphs: Observe time to first meaningful choice, variety of moment-to-moment activity, clarity of failure, remaining personal effort, solo completion rate and use of voluntary cooperation. Record results separately at 1/2/5/10/30 connected clients. The session-duration examples are targets to test.

sections.title: Production boundary
paragraphs: Create the smallest connected playable route before producing six regions. All five vocations remain final design requirements; showing three early prototype choices is honest staging, not cancellation of the other two.

pages.title: State ownership and authority
pages.summary: Every meaningful mutable fact has one writer, a lifetime and a recovery rule.

sections.title: Definitions are not player state
paragraphs: A definition describes permitted data: a recipe, item, vocation or authored region stage. It may be loaded by many actors and clients. A runtime instance describes what is currently happening. A durable record describes what must survive restart. A projection is a limited copy used by an actor or interface; displaying it does not make that viewer the writer.

rows: Owner-only private character view; approved public identity
Validated zone/service command → receipt; reconnect pulls canonical revision.
Region actor and public GameState summaries
Health, cast window, local movement, AI
Validated input/ability commands; checkpoint/death policy governs recovery.
Fence each durable write; single-use activation or newer-epoch recovery.
No game persistence; reopen and pull state.
Derived from approved action/facing; no reward mutation.
Shared social responsibility in the initial service
Permission-revalidated commands; reconnect reads current membership.
Zone clock projection and visual tints
All zones derive from the same committed schedule; client clock ignored.
Server admission and current zone initialization
Shared database or client UI owner.
Owned request route and local input/widgets
Public identity, approved private projections and selected GAS ownership

Canonical durable writes and lease/receipt validation

sections.title: Initialization order
steps: Authenticate and resolve the account/character without trusting client-supplied ownership.
Reserve or validate a current lease, verify content/schema compatibility and read durable records.
Create the server body and initialize components/ability owner-avatar references.
Publish public/owner-only snapshots. Bind local view listeners then pull state; accept only newer revisions.
Enable commands only after hydration. On death/travel, cancel old actions, unbind observers and fence or release ownership as appropriate.

sections.title: Visibility is not authority
paragraphs: A replicated value may be public without being client-editable. A BlueprintCallable method may only submit a request. Each command validates ownership, permissions and current lease on the server and at the durable write boundary. Cosmetic animation and UI events signal or display a completed change; they cannot create it.

sections.title: Evidence boundary
paragraphs: The framework role comparison is consistent with Epic’s networking overview; the exact owner allocation and durable service topology are proposed Briarwake architecture. Installed game/plugin code was not compiled.

pages.title: Transactions, receipts and durable outcomes
pages.summary: Commit value changes once, then publish replay-safe projections.

sections.title: What the boundary promises
paragraphs: Recommended initial choice: one small service with a transactional store owns character value, world contributions and durable receipts. Technology/provider selection remains open. Do not introduce distributed transactions across many services before the single-boundary route works.

Transport delivery may repeat or fail. The design aims for one durable effect per accepted operation, not a promise that messages are delivered exactly once. A receipt and uniqueness constraints make repeated delivery safe.

rows: Same ID retained for an unknown-outcome retry.
Known handler; not a client-defined function.
Never accept another owner simply because the payload names it.
Current writer epoch checked inside the mutation transaction.
Map of affected aggregate IDs to integer revisions
Reject stale decisions rather than overwriting newer values.
Positive counts, valid IDs, range/state/permission checks.
Canonical hash of semantic request fields
Exclude transport credentials; include recipe/amount/relevant expected revisions.

sections.title: Commit sequence
steps: Authenticate and apply rate limits. Resolve the command’s character scope and content definition. Reject malformed requests before expensive work.
Look up an existing receipt under (character/account scope, operation type, RequestId). Return it only to the authorized owner. If the semantic payload digest differs, reject RequestIdentityConflict.
In the transaction, lock or compare affected records in a deterministic order. Recheck the current session epoch and expected revisions here—not only before making the service call.
Plan all changes: material/currency debits, item capacity and instance creation, quest/mastery/project updates. Validate the complete plan before any commit.
Commit the plan, domain uniqueness keys, receipt and outbox entry atomically. Store the returned instance IDs and exact committed revisions in the receipt.
Publish privacy-filtered projections from the outbox. Consumers accept revisions idempotently; delivery may repeat. A crash between commit and publish is recovered by the pending outbox.

A client/server that lost the response queries the receipt or retries the same semantic request. A fresh lease may query an older committed receipt for the same authenticated character; it may not authorize a new write using an old epoch.

sections.title: Example: one fitting, not two
sections.code:
ILLUSTRATIVE TRANSACTION FLOW — NOT RUNNABLE GAME CODE
Scope = (char-bw-forge, Craft, request-fit-001)
Inputs before: IronOre=3; SalvagePlate=1
Recipe: recipe.watch-fitting@1 → WatchFitting=1
Validate current lease epoch, inventory revision and station entitlement
Commit: Ore=0; Plate=0; ItemInstanceId=server-generated-id
Commit together: mastery increment + receipt + outbox
Lost response → retry request-fit-001 → return original instance ID
Different RequestId with empty inputs → InsufficientMaterials
Same RequestId with changed recipe/count → RequestIdentityConflict

sections.title: Reservations and cancellation
paragraphs: The initial craft is an immediate atomic operation. Timed crafting needs a durable reservation only if ingredients are reserved across a delay. Reserved items cannot also be sold, equipped into a conflicting state, traded or consumed. The reservation has a state machine: Reserved → Completed or Cancelled, with one terminal transaction. A cancellation cannot refund inputs after completion.

A spinner timing out or an actor disappearing is not sufficient evidence to refund. Query the reservation/receipt first. If storage is unavailable, expose PendingSave/RecoveryPending and prevent competing value mutations until the outcome is known.

sections.title: Uniqueness beyond requests
paragraphs: New client-generated request IDs must not bypass domain uniqueness. Use permanent or appropriately retained guards for (EncounterInstanceId, CharacterId, RewardVersion), (CastId, CharacterId), (SiteId, Generation, ClaimId), (CharacterId, QuestId, completion generation) and unique contribution identities. Receipt retention alone is insufficient if old domain events can be replayed after receipts are pruned.

sections.title: Reject, retry and compensate are different
paragraphs: A validation rejection has no committed value changes. A transient service failure before a known commit can be retried with the same identity. An unknown outcome must be queried. A compensation is a new audited transaction after a known committed outcome; it must never blindly replay an old snapshot over newer character progress.

A definitive stale-revision rejection followed by a revised player choice is a new semantic request. Do not change fields under the old RequestId. Authentication failures must not create unauthenticated access to another character’s receipt.

rows: No value change; same request may execute later.
Either transaction aborts or a commit is queryable; no partial debit.
Receipt returns original result after reconnect.
Persistent outbox eventually republishes committed projection.
Views converge by revision and do not grant rewards.
Old source mutation fails its in-transaction epoch check.
Restore into isolation, verify revision/receipt consistency, and require an operational recovery plan before admitting live clients.

sections.title: Implementation gap
paragraphs: This document specifies a proposed contract. Concrete schemas, transaction implementation, database choice, transport authentication, production retention and fault-injection results remain future work. No database was created by this package.

pages.title: Per-character zone transfers
pages.summary: Move one character between authoritative zone processes without displacing everyone else.

sections.title: Choose the correct travel boundary
paragraphs: Epic documents that whole-server ServerTravel brings connected clients to the new world. Briarwake’s per-character biome crossing therefore requires a separate destination process and a validated client reconnection coordinated with durable ownership. Seamless travel within one server is not a cross-server database or identity protocol.

Recommended initial choice: Thornmere and Elderwood are separate dedicated processes on ports 7777 and 7778 in the development fixture, with one small directory/transfer responsibility alongside persistence.

sections.title: Transfer state machine
sections.code:
SOURCE_ACTIVE(epoch e)
  → PREPARING (stop new actions; drain/reconcile pending durable work)
  → DESTINATION_RESERVED (short-lived capacity reservation)
  → IN_TRANSIT(epoch e+1; source writer fenced)
  → DESTINATION_ACTIVE(epoch e+1; ticket consumed)
  → SOURCE_RETIRED

Before fencing failure: cancel preparation and resume epoch e if still valid.
After fencing failure: service recovery claims a NEW epoch; never revive e.

sections.title: Protocol and actor responsibilities
steps: The player reaches a validated gate. Source checks destination eligibility, route unlock, safe spawn, current lease and no incompatible action.
Freeze new gameplay/value commands and reconcile in-flight durable operations by receipt. Do not capture a snapshot while a craft may still commit unnoticed.
Reserve destination capacity. Record TransferId, CharacterId, source/destination zone IDs, content version and a short expiration.

Commit the verified handoff snapshot and fence source ownership in the same authoritative transition. Increment the character epoch and enter InTransit; old source commands now fail their transactional epoch check.
Issue a short-lived single-use opaque ticket bound to character, account, destination, transfer and new epoch. Keep bearer material out of logs, screenshots and public session advertisements.
Instruct only that client to connect to the reserved destination. The loading screen displays progress but has no ownership authority.

The destination authenticates the client and atomically consumes the ticket/reservation while acquiring the active lease for the new epoch. It validates the arrival cell, content and snapshot revision before possession.
Initialize the new body and subscriptions, then activate commands. The source retires its body after terminal confirmation or fencing; visual destruction is not the fence itself.

rows: Cancel reservation/preparation, retain valid source lease and resume safely.
Client drops after fencing but before ticket consumption
Keep InTransit durable state; reconnect queries coordinator, not cached source address.
Ticket stays consumed; recovery uses the canonical checkpoint/receipt state and a newer lease epoch.
Consumption and timeout recovery race through one compare/commit decision; only one wins.
Admit as a new authoritative session with a newer epoch, not by unfreezing the old body.
Source sends a late item command
Persistence rejects the old epoch even if that actor is still alive.
Return transfer terminal state or reject; no second possession/lease.
Do not activate incompatible content; recover to a validated safe checkpoint through the coordinator.

sections.title: Data contract
paragraphs: Record_Transfer includes TransferId, authenticated CharacterId, source/destination identities, snapshot revision, policy/content versions, token digest, reservation expiry and terminal result. Record_SessionLease includes CharacterId, owner server instance, epoch, expiry and status. No Actor pointer crosses processes or becomes a database key.

Every durable mutation checks the lease at commit time. Merely stopping input or deleting the source Pawn cannot prevent an already queued command from committing. Fencing must be a persisted check enforced by the same mutation boundary.

sections.title: Two-client fixture
steps: Launch Thornmere and Elderwood dedicated processes only after actual game builds exist. Connect two separate clients to Thornmere.
Client A crosses the north gate; client B remains in Thornmere. Assert B’s connection/map is unchanged.
On A verify character/vocation/appearance/item instance IDs and region state. The active lease table contains one owner for A.
Inject failure at each named protocol step, then repeat with stale tickets, repeated transfer requests and an old-source craft.
Observe one durable terminal outcome and a safe reconnection path. Packet travel success alone does not pass the ownership test.

sections.title: Evidence and scope
paragraphs: This is a proposed protocol requiring implementation, secure transport and failure testing. No transfer coordinator or dedicated server was executed. The engine travel distinction was checked against UE-TRAVEL; all Briarwake service APIs remain custom future work.

sections.title: ADR-001 · Naming override
paragraphs: Committed requirement from the latest user instruction: the game is Briarwake and the destination is evanmcpheron/mmo_docs. The original master prompt is preserved unchanged as evidence. New native plans use Source/Briarwake rather than Source/RPG. This is a new game/module plan, not a claim that existing native files were renamed.

sections.title: ADR-002 · Slice B moves to Phase 19
paragraphs: The source schedules Slice B after Phase 18 but requires the cartography route implemented in Phase 19. This guide places the Slice B acceptance checkpoint after Phase 19. It does not silently move or delete Wayfinder content. All roadmap/slice references use the revised checkpoint.

sections.title: ADR-003 · Minimal services before full systems
paragraphs: Slice B also requires a merchant and contribution board before the full Phase 25 economy and Phase 22/23 region work. Phase 13 introduces only baseline fixed NPC supply/repair/commission services through the existing durable command path. Phase 15 introduces the minimal durable region/project schema and board needed by the Forgekeeper repair outcome. Later phases extend those exact owners/IDs instead of creating second implementations.

sections.title: ADR-004 · Early combat fixture, later specialization
paragraphs: Phase 09 uses a minimal basic melee/ranged ability fixture. Phase 12 supplies the full discipline/talent data and purchase UI. Do not require a not-yet-created specialization definition merely to prove one server-authorized dummy hit.

sections.title: ADR-005 · Incomplete input gates stay visible

The art and plugin audit pages record brief-reported leads and exact next verification steps, but they do not invent archive paths, line numbers, dimensions or compilation results. The register is provisional and non-exhaustive until those audits and detailed content authoring are complete.

README.txt and AGENTS.md were read, and architecture, Phase 03 and E_EquipmentSlot content were sampled. The HTML connector responses were truncated. A direct clone failed because the runtime could not resolve github.com. Therefore this is a sampled crosswalk, not a completed full-repository audit.
The source README reports 163 current assets, 12 phases and 19 systems. Those are historical reference-repository counts, not counts for Briarwake or proof of compiled game code.

sections.title: Never rewrite the reference
paragraphs: No writes were sent to game_docs. The new guide uses original text, structures and design contracts rather than republishing an entire source repository. Audit the remaining source pages before claiming exhaustive migration coverage.

sections.title: Native implementation standard
paragraphs: Use descriptive names, explicit invariants and small cohesive components. Prefer composition over a universal Actor superclass. Server transaction primitives are shared across crafting/quest/economy/project changes, while actual domain validation remains readable and separate.

pages.title: Architecture overview
pages.summary: A small authoritative topology with explicit durable boundaries.

sections.title: Recommended initial topology
sections.code:
CLIENT

sections.title: Scale only after measurement

sections.title: Quick diagnostic
paragraphs: Ask where the fact survives a zone crash, which one writer can commit it, how a client requests change, what revision/receipt prevents replay and how a new actor rebuilds its view. If the answer is “the widget” or “the animation finished” for money, items, quests or regional stages, the design is incorrect.

sections.title: Required evidence first

Briarwake’s installed 5.8.3 source, actual targets and plugin builds are not available here. Follow the official mechanism, then verify the exact local build configuration and generated executable paths.

sections.title: Future setup sequence
steps: In the future game, enable verified required modules/plugins. Create the native runtime classes and the actual server/client build targets; none is supplied by this documentation package.
Set Maps & Modes → Server Default Map to the intended authored map; keep the client frontend separate. Assign the custom GameMode/Controller/PlayerState/default pawn classes.
Build Development Server and Development Client using the verified toolchain; cook the required maps and dependencies for both configurations.
Run the headless process with a log and explicit port, then connect two separate clients. Do not describe multiple PIE viewports as packaged process/provider proof.
For Phase 07, run a second server on another port and use the custom verified transfer coordinator. Register actual process identities and capacity without publishing credentials.

pages.title: Vocation choice and changing policy
pages.summary: Meaningful specialization without an irreversible beginner mistake.

sections.title: Character creation contract
paragraphs: Committed requirement: one and only one primary vocation is selected for every playable character. The creator shows an active choice’s typical actions, pace/difficulty, products, world contribution, combat synergy and boundaries. Unsupported exclusive costumes are not part of the promise.

Committed requirement: select one permanent combat class through UCombatDisciplineDefinition and one permanent faction separately from the changeable vocation. Every available class supports every available vocation. Combat level/XP, class abilities and purchased combat talents cannot change when retraining a vocation.

sections.title: Base proficiency versus specialization
paragraphs: All characters can fight, explore, complete quests, gather common materials, fish at basic spots and use essential NPC services. The chosen vocation controls advanced techniques, superior outcome control, specialist recipe permissions and its own quest/mastery graph. NPC commissions provide required cross-vocation goods at attainable authored prices.

rows: After the introduction and three varied vocation contracts. This is an activity commitment, not a real-time daily/login gate.
An appropriate trainer; the server validates range, eligibility and pending transactions.

All items, permanent quest outcomes, faction allegiance, Living Regions credit and combat progression remain. Every trained vocation retains its own XP, derived level, mastery XP/points, purchased skills/talents, learned recipes, techniques and accomplishments.
Advanced abilities/techniques requiring the old active vocation are disabled; items remain subject to their ordinary use/bind rules.

A never-trained vocation gets one Level-1 record at its defined initial XP and introductory mentor access. A returning vocation restores its saved record, not Level 1. Starter-kit and one-time unlock/mastery outcomes cannot replay.
An explicit affordable retraining contract and a published currency fee; exact fee is a tuning decision still to author. No punitive item wipe.
Complete three varied contracts in the new vocation before another switch. No mandatory calendar wait.

No pending trade/craft/transfer or unresolved durable work. Commit active VocationId, keyed progression, any existing authored retraining debit, change receipt and outbox together. Rebuild runtime permissions from that committed revision before enabling vocation actions; runtime handles are not stored in the transaction.
Additional slots may offer another vocation, but alts are never required for the story or mastery.

sections.title: Migration and exploit tests
paragraphs: Switch away and back, reconnect during confirmation, replay the change and try an old specialist recipe. Old progress remains; inactive permissions cannot be used; free kit/recipe grants do not repeat. A content update must not reinterpret a stored vocation ID by array position.

sections.title: Remaining decisions
paragraphs: The exact fee, contract list, full mastery-node graphs and real pacing need authoring and playtesting. The initial policy is a recommended choice, not a preexisting engine feature or a user-approved final balance table.

sections.title: Server-authoritative ChangeVocation contract
paragraphs: ChangeVocation(Envelope, TargetVocationId, TrainerId) is a proposed Briarwake operation routed by the existing owned controller/NPC service through UDurableStateClient; it is not an Unreal API or a new transaction framework. Envelope uses OperationType=ChangeVocation, RequestId, authenticated character scope, LeaseEpoch, ExpectedRevisions and ContentVersion. Its semantic digest includes TargetVocationId, TrainerId, the decision revisions and pinned content, not renewed transport credentials.

Keep the established provisional trainer policy above: introduction and three varied contracts, an appropriate trainer, the authored affordable retraining contract/fee, and three varied contracts before another switch. Exact fee/content remains unapproved tuning. Do not invent another fee, cooldown, penalty, prerequisite or human-player dependency. Missing required authored policy/definitions blocks that integration test rather than making up values.
steps: Authenticate the character; reject impersonation. Look up (character scope, ChangeVocation, RequestId) before current trainer/eligibility/revision checks. Return an authorized matching committed receipt unchanged; a changed semantic payload returns RequestIdentityConflict. A fresh lease may read an older receipt; it cannot authorize a new write with an old epoch.

For a new mutation, validate the current authoritative session lease and live trainer interaction/range, the existing retraining eligibility and fee policy, and the requested available UVocationDefinition. Same active target returns AlreadyActive with no fee, progression change or repeated grants. Prepare required versioned definitions before entering the commit boundary.

Within the existing transaction lock/compare the character and any affected fee aggregate in deterministic order. Recheck LeaseEpoch, ExpectedRevisions, content, trainer authorization and eligibility. Reject IncompatiblePendingOperation for pending trade/craft/transfer or unresolved value/XP work; do not copy a snapshot while another durable result is unknown.

Stage the full next Record_Character, preserving Progression.Combat and every existing Progression.Vocations entry. If TargetVocationId has never been trained in a validated schema, add one entry at InitialXP with derived Level 1 and defined initial values. Otherwise reuse its saved entry byte-for-byte; do not rerun its starter or earned unlock grants.

Set only VocationId to the target. Compute the target permission plan from its committed-history candidate and authored definitions. Validate unique grants and preserve class abilities/talents, faction, inventory items, permanent quest outcomes and Living Regions contributions. The only permitted unrelated debit is the already-authored retraining fee, if applicable.

Commit the staged record, one Revision increment, any existing authored debit, permanent domain uniqueness guards, Record_CommandReceipt and outbox atomically. The receipt records old/new vocation IDs and exact committed revisions. No receipt, fee, history or active selector may commit alone.

After commit, rebuild only vocation-sourced permissions/modifiers on the server from the new revision; gate vocation commands until hydration is complete. Publish the permitted public identity subset and owner-only histories via the existing outbox/projection route. Clients ignore older state revisions; an old receipt is historical evidence, not a command to restore its old active vocation.

sections.title: Active permissions, independent awards and recovery
paragraphs: LearnedRecipeIds, purchased skills/talents, techniques and accomplishments stay in each inactive entry. Specialist availability requires both current VocationId and the newly active saved progression/definition prerequisites. Remove or disable only handles/modifiers sourced exclusively from the former vocation; preserve class/equipment/general-activity grants. Deduplicate by stable grant source and authored ability/effect identity. Widgets and copied client permission lists are never authority.

Revalidate active vocation permission on authoritative ability activation and crafting acceptance/commit, including delayed requests with old UI or grant handles. Switching cannot make an old specialist recipe legal. Preserve general gathering, basic fishing, combat and essential NPC alternatives available to every character. Rebuilds are deterministic set reconciliation, not additive reward delivery.

CombatXP and targeted VocationXP are independently authored, validated and stored. Quest rewards may specify both separately under one unique completion transaction. Purchased combat talents spend only combat points; vocation purchases spend only that vocation’s mastery points. An accepted activity names its target VocationId and content/revision context; serialize/reconcile its award before switching, never redirect delayed XP to a different active vocation.

Before commit an interruption leaves the original active vocation and histories intact. After commit, a lost response/reconnect/restart resolves through the same receipt and outbox. Repeated delivery cannot grant starter items, mastery points or modifiers again. Two competing changes with the same expected Revision yield one commit and one StaleRevision rejection; no two active vocations. Replaying an earlier accepted change after a later switch returns its original receipt without changing current state.

Respawn, logout/reconnect and per-character zone transfer hydrate all vocation histories from Record_Character, then rebuild the active permission set once. Fence the old zone and reject late commands under its old epoch. Never save progression in the Pawn, UI, Data Asset or a second progression owner.

sections.title: Talent contract
paragraphs: Each node declares a stable ID, point cost, prerequisite node IDs, exclusive branch group where applicable, granted ability/effect ID and respec policy. Purchases validate budget and prerequisites in the service; the zone rebuilds permitted GAS grants from the committed build revision.

Suggested first meaningful choice is between a defensive utility and a situational damage/control tool, not dozens of indistinguishable percentage bonuses. Exact nodes, level tables and complete class balance are still to be authored.

sections.title: Creator and tutorial
paragraphs: Committed requirement: choose exactly one available combat discipline during character creation and store its stable DefinitionId as CombatDisciplineId. This combat class is permanent. Every available class supports every vocation and valid faction; no vocation change changes class, combat XP/level, abilities or purchased combat talents. Respec only redistributes talents within the existing class under its current policy.

Introduce a basic art-supported combat action in the tutorial and let the player learn the difference from vocation. The prototype may offer only currently integrated disciplines. Final-system documentation still owes all four specified skill trees and their tested solo paths.

sections.title: Rebuild and respec tests
paragraphs: Respawn, equipment swap, travel, reconnect and respec must not duplicate attribute modifiers or ability grants. Remove old grant/effect handles and apply the new validated build once. Never write independent cooldown logic inside ability-bar widgets.

sections.title: GAS boundary
paragraphs: GAS is the recommended framework for attributes, abilities, effects and cooldowns after installed-version validation. Quest rewards, persistence, crafting, professions, party membership and realm allocation remain separate explicit responsibilities.

sections.title: Independent combat progression and write protection
paragraphs: Record_Character.Progression.Combat owns combat TotalXP, pinned DefinitionVersion, purchased talent IDs and unspent combat points. Derive level from its validated curve, not vocation level; Combat 40 / Forgekeeper 5 and Combat 10 / Hearthkeeper 30 are valid unless a particular authored activity explicitly states a requirement. Vocation mastery points cannot buy combat talents.

Reject any post-creation CombatDisciplineId mutation at the authoritative durable boundary, including a generic record update or forged client payload. No class-change NPC, reset token, alternate active class or multiclass system is introduced. Returning to a vocation restores only that vocation’s progression; class grants remain associated with the permanently selected definition.

pages.title: Solo-to-30 parity specification
pages.summary: Preserve essential access and stable credited progress while making cooperation useful.

sections.title: What parity does and does not mean
paragraphs: Committed requirement: one human can complete the required narrative, essential crafting tiers, profession mastery and critical regional improvements. Comparable personal time-to-value is the target; identical completion speed and identical social experience are not promised.

NPC baseline supplies, commissions, alternate objectives and constrained mechanic helpers fill real dependencies. Optional guild chat or player trade naturally requires other people; the story must not require successfully performing those social actions.

sections.title: Recommended population-sensitive project model
paragraphs: Separate essential project work from optional reinforcements. EssentialTarget = 12 illustrative contribution units, fixed and achievable through every character’s available routes. OptionalTarget(n) = 8 + 2 × ceil(log2(n + 1)), where n is clamped to 1–30 engaged distinct accounts from a bounded 24-hour server window.

At stage activation, persist n, policy version, EssentialTarget, OptionalTarget and objective conversion rules. Never retune an active stage because of logins/logouts. More accounts cannot lower a target. There is no deadline or offline decay; optional reinforcement remains finite and can also be finished alone.

An engaged account must have completed multiple distinct eligible actions; repeated logins, chat or movement alone do not count. Count once per account, not per character. This reduces simple alt inflation but is not proof against multi-account abuse; record abuse tests and operational limits.

sections.title: Personal effort and late arrival
paragraphs: The personal-value milestone is four varied accepted contribution units in the test model, independent of live population. After the permanent project closes, a separately authored maintenance/research contract offers equivalent personal vocation/reputation value without undoing construction. A stale donation to a completed stage rejects before debit; the player reviews the new objective rather than being silently charged for a different one.

pages.title: Briarwake: world and story
pages.summary: An original frontier setting organized around rebuilding useful paths.

sections.title: Premise
paragraphs: Recommended original setting: the Briarwake is a recurring surge of unnatural growth around abandoned waystones. It exposes old paths and ruins while disturbing creatures and supply routes. Settlements survive through skilled outings, preparation and restoration—not by waiting for a chosen hero to solve everything alone in a cutscene.

sections.title: The frontier’s history
paragraphs: Long before Thornmere, a network of signal bells and maintained roads linked the basin, forest, fen, heights, mountain and coast. Its keepers disagreed over whether the waystones should be sealed or studied. The neglected network now fails in different ways across the six regions. The player discovers that repairing useful links and understanding the warnings matters as much as defeating the immediate threats.

rows: Protect crossings, supply crews and shared routes
Repair plans, safe-route services and visible contribution recognition.
Feed settlements and preserve practical local knowledge
Menu variations, garden commissions and optional seasonal gatherings.
Study waystones, field clues and fictional afflictions

sections.title: Six connected regional arcs
paragraphs: Thornmere teaches the systems. Elderwood joins the vocation contributions at North Road and Bellroot Vault. Siltfen tests water/food/research choices. Cairnstep emphasizes supply and supports. Hollowpeak develops salvage and old plans. Galehaven concludes the route network through beacon/ferry restoration.

sections.title: Permanent history and repeatable adventure
paragraphs: Major construction remains complete. Repeatable threats, maintenance contracts, new discoveries and optional reinforcement provide renewed activity without resetting a village to punish absent players. First-arrival recognition is optional; later players retain meaningful personal arcs.

sections.title: Content boundaries
paragraphs: All names, factions and story summaries here are proposed original content, not proof of implemented maps/dialogue. Complete scene scripts, quest definitions and localization text remain future authoring work. No Tolkien characters, geography, plots or distinctive designs are part of the specification.

pages.title: Data-driven content production
pages.summary: Add ordinary content through reviewed definitions and existing systems.

sections.title: A new item is not a new manager
paragraphs: Create an item definition with a stable ID, reviewed stack/bind/slot/affix rules and an audited appearance key or explicit nonvisual fallback. Register it once. Assign its actual consumers: recipe, loot table, merchant, quest or project. A definition with no use is not implemented content.

sections.title: A new quest is an objective graph
paragraphs: Choose existing objective types: kill, gather, fish, plant/harvest, craft, deliver, talk, interact, research, scout/map, rescue, defend, dungeon and region contribution. Author prerequisites, localized text and success/rejection/reward rules. The quest evaluator consumes validated receipts; do not add one Blueprint class for each ordinary quest.

sections.title: A new biome is a checked content bundle
steps: Declare geography, outward and return gates, hub/service set and a complete solo route.
Audit/acquire the actual art and define import/pivot/tile/collision requirements. Missing art blocks visual acceptance but does not justify claiming a nonexistent pack.
Author tile layers, walkability, eligible resource sites, fishing polygons, plots, enemies and NPC services.
Create quest/discovery/project definitions with stable IDs and content versions; register every concrete asset before use.
Run validator checks for references, duplicate IDs, unreachable objectives, invalid cells, unsupported appearance/action combinations and graph cycles.
Test one-human completion, two-client shared-state/travel, crowded contention, restart, content migration and rollback policy before release.

sections.title: Clock and weather
paragraphs: Recommended initial choice: persist a realm epoch, game-time rate, weather seed/schedule version and authored transitions. Zone servers derive coherent local effects from the same authoritative source. Do not let a client clock or tint authorize a rare catch. Use controlled server-clock fixtures to test transitions, and provide alternate accessible windows for essential objectives.

sections.title: Do not silently expand scope
paragraphs: A new ordinary recipe, item, NPC service or quest should normally fit existing schemas. A genuinely new mechanic needs a reviewed system/owner/transaction/UI/art/test contract and registry update first. Housing, PvP and freeform simulation are not ordinary data entries in this committed version.

sections.title: Definition of content completion
paragraphs: A registered page is not enough. The content is assigned, loaded, reachable through the player route, tested for valid and rejected paths, recovered after restart and proven compatible with its actual art. This package supplies the pipeline and initial fixtures, not a finished six-biome content database.

pages.title: Paper2D import and 2D map configuration
pages.summary: Verify one real source sheet before expanding the import pipeline.

sections.title: Prerequisites
paragraphs: Official Paper2D documentation describes enabling the plugin through Edit → Plugins and restarting the Editor. The following is a version-sensitive workflow to check in the actual target installation, not a completed import.

sections.title: One audited character
steps: Read the creator guide and identify one complete body/outfit/action/facing set. Record exact archive paths, dimensions and frame spacing; do not infer frame size from the filename.

Enable Paper2D, restart and import the selected textures into Content/Game/Art. Open each Texture asset and verify nearest filtering/pixel-art settings, no unwanted mip blur and consistent color handling. Inspect actual option names in the installed Editor.
Extract sprites using the documented grid or transparent regions. Verify the first and last frames manually; automatic extraction can incorrectly split tools or transparent gaps.
Set a consistent pixels-per-unit value and shared foot anchor. Build the four idle and four walk flipbooks using only audited frames and creator timing.
Render each layer on the same animation clock. Test a full cycle with large tools, hat and cloak; a layer cannot select its own independent pose frame.
Open L_BriarwakePreview, switch all four facings, zoom within bounds and compare foot placement. Repeat from a remote client after the network phase.

sections.title: Tiles and collision
paragraphs: Create a TileSet from an acquired atlas, assign correct tile dimensions/margins and inspect collision shapes per blocked tile. Place ground, obstacle and overhead layers separately. Test a fixed orthographic camera with sprites and tiles aligned to the flat gameplay plane. An invisible collision floor is implementation support, not a 3D visual environment.

sections.title: Occlusion test
paragraphs: Walk in front of and behind a tree trunk, roof edge, doorway and bridge support. Use ground-contact position for Y sorting; canopy/roof overlays use separate intentional layers. Cosmetic hop lift must not change the contact coordinate used for sort/collision. Test adjacent feet positions for flicker and long tool clipping.

sections.title: Stop condition
paragraphs: Do not accept visual quality until actual source sheets, pivots, sorting and packaged rendering are checked. Missing jump/swim/weapon actions remain listed in the art backlog.

pages.title: Facing selection and paper-doll synchronization
pages.summary: Eight movement sectors do not create missing diagonal artwork.

sections.title: Four-facing rule
paragraphs: Recommended initial mapping: N→North, NE→North, E→East, SE→East, S→South, SW→South, W→West, NW→West. At a sector boundary keep the previous facing until a small configurable hysteresis is exceeded; idle preserves the last valid facing. Aim may override movement only under a declared action rule. These are design choices, not engine defaults.

sections.title: One pose clock
paragraphs: UCharacterAppearanceComponent receives a presentation snapshot: action, four-facing, shared sequence/time, appearance revision. The body and supported overlays resolve compatible pose frames together. PaperZD integration is conditional on inspecting its installed source/sequence/AnimBP APIs. Do not name guessed native Blueprint nodes as working APIs.

sections.title: Gameplay and notifies
paragraphs: GAS/server action windows authorize hits, costs and catches. Animation notifies may play footsteps, a splash or impact visual, but a missing notify must not cancel a committed reward or create a duplicate one. Remote animation consumes authoritative state with local visual interpolation.

sections.title: Future eight-facing expansion
paragraphs: Create a versioned direction-capability matrix for every body, outfit, hair, cloak, tool and action. New directional frames must exist for compatible combinations before enabling them. Keep four-facing fallback for old appearances. Migrate catalog keys without changing owned item IDs or ability mechanics.

sections.title: Regression fixture
paragraphs: Test each action with a hat, cloak and long tool; change equipment during idle and interrupt an action mid-frame. Reconnect in another zone. Verify shared pose, stable pivots and no gameplay dependency on the animation graph. True diagonal art, six-facing art and eight-facing art are separate authoring work—not synthetic claims about four sheets.

pages.title: C++ and Blueprint engineering standard
pages.summary: Implement one authoritative rule once; expose bounded authoring and observation to Blueprint.

sections.title: Native scope
paragraphs: C++ owns reusable movement/action components, server validation, IDs, transaction routing, authoritative combat integration, replication conditions, lifecycle and cancellation. Blueprint selects approved definitions and composes presentation. The guide proposes APIs; none of the custom types or methods is supplied by the engine.

sections.title: Blueprint exposure
paragraphs: Use EditDefaultsOnly for immutable authoring inputs, BlueprintReadOnly for views and BlueprintCallable for narrow validated command entry points. Cosmetic BlueprintImplementableEvent hooks may react to committed state; they cannot award currency, skill points or catches. Editable properties do not authorize client mutation.

sections.title: Lifecycle contract
steps: Create only current-phase types and compile the native project before selecting them as Blueprint parents.
Assign required definitions in the actual consumer. Validate null and unsupported version cases during initialization.
Bind the observer once, then pull the current snapshot. Make teardown remove the same binding and invalidate pending presentation callbacks.
On possession/zone changes, replace the body view without duplicating durable character records. Reject stale generation/lease callbacks.
Keep error codes stable and log request/receipt/revision IDs without tokens or private message contents.

sections.title: Maintainability
paragraphs: Prefer descriptive names, shallow inheritance and composition for shared gathering/crafting behavior. Five vocations are data and permission policies, not five duplicated resource systems. Avoid a universal manager or global event bus. Do not implement a second cooldown/attribute framework alongside GAS.

sections.title: Review checklist
bullets: One authoritative writer per fact; immutable definition distinct from owned instance and view.
Server-side permissions and lease fencing at commit, not only at command arrival.
Failure leaves no unexplained debit; duplicates return the same committed result.
Actual existing consumers assign and invoke the feature; no disconnected shells.
Missing art, plugin API assumptions and unrun tests are explicitly recorded.

pages.title: Operations, recovery and population testing
pages.summary: Treat durability failures as state reconciliation problems, not user-interface retries.

sections.title: Controlled environments
paragraphs: Keep development, test and production identities/configuration separate. Credentials belong in environment-specific secret storage, never client packages, this manual or logs. Provider choice and concrete deployment automation require a separate verified implementation.

sections.title: Backups and migrations
paragraphs: Version records and content catalogs. Rehearse restoring a backup into an isolated store, replaying only supported committed receipts/outbox work and validating inventory/region/session consistency. Record recovery point and recovery time from an actual rehearsal. Backing up without restore testing is not a recovery proof.

rows: Reject or retain a known pending operation; do not display a durable success.
Resolve same receipt without repeat debit.
Expire/fence the old lease, admit one recovery session.
Reject or migrate through a versioned reviewed map; do not silently reinterpret IDs.
Match compatible zone/client/content versions or deny admission cleanly.
Rate-limit by authenticated scope, log bounded diagnostics and preserve unrelated players’ progress.

sections.title: Population fixtures
paragraphs: Run 1, 2, 5, 10 and 30 actual connected clients with active combat/gather/vendor/region/social/travel interactions. Record hardware, build SHA, connection count, latency/loss, scenario duration, server CPU/frame time, network traffic and persistence command latency. Budgets are proposed only after a baseline is measured.

sections.title: Privacy and moderation
paragraphs: Document block/report flows, permission checks, account bans and admin audit. Avoid public account IDs, inventory contents, tokens or private chat in replicated state/logs. Data retention and deletion policy require decisions appropriate to the actual service; this manual does not supply legal compliance certification.

sections.title: Runtime evidence
paragraphs: No server deployment, backup restore, game packet-loss test or 30-client benchmark was run during this documentation task.

pages.title: Population scaling: model and measurement
pages.summary: Keep essential work stable; evaluate optional capacity through a frozen activation policy.

sections.title: Model contract
paragraphs: The proposed essential target is 12 credited units, independent of online population. Optional reinforcement target is 8 + 2 × ceil(log2(n + 1)) with engaged accounts n clamped to 1–30. Persist n, targets and policy version at activation; subsequent login/logout does not retune that project.

sections.title: What the included simulation proves
paragraphs: The arithmetic script checks 1/2/5/10/30 values, monotonic optional effort, a fixed essential target and frozen goals under changing population. It does not simulate real players, encounter AI, network load, fun, completion time or a production economy.

sections.title: Required runtime extension
paragraphs: Exercise alternate solo contribution categories and per-character repeatable maintenance after a shared project is already complete. Measure personal time-to-value and stalls for all five vocations. Test alts, inactive logins, bots, rushed engagement windows and 30 people at the same last objective.

sections.title: Acceptance boundary
paragraphs: Do not select final balance based only on the arithmetic passing. A game test must establish ingredient availability, accessible encounters, fair contention and understandable remaining effort.

pages.title: Glossary
pages.summary: Definitions used by the Briarwake ownership and build contracts.

sections.title: Actor
paragraphs: A live object in a world, such as a creature or resource site. Destroying it must not erase a durable record.

sections.title: Pawn / Character
paragraphs: A controllable body; Character adds movement-oriented engine facilities. Neither is the account database.

sections.title: Component
paragraphs: Reusable behavior attached to an Actor. Use it for a focused responsibility, not a duplicate model.

sections.title: Interface
paragraphs: A shared callable contract for otherwise unrelated types. It does not create authority or storage.

sections.title: GameMode
paragraphs: Server-only rules/admission for the current world.

sections.title: GameState
paragraphs: Replicated public state for the current world, not a durable cross-server database.

sections.title: PlayerController
paragraphs: Owned input and command/UI routing. Validate gameplay requests server-side.

sections.title: PlayerState
paragraphs: Replicated per-player runtime state; privacy depends on which fields are sent to which connections.

sections.title: GameInstance
paragraphs: Process-lifetime coordination across ordinary local travel. Each process has its own; it is not shared realm truth.

sections.title: Server RPC
paragraphs: A client-to-server request through an owned network object. It is not evidence that its payload is valid.

sections.title: Replication
paragraphs: Server-selected state sent to appropriate clients. Persisting and replicating are different operations.

sections.title: Prediction
paragraphs: Permitted temporary client response before server confirmation, with correction/reconciliation.

sections.title: Data Asset
paragraphs: Authored immutable definition data. A recipe definition is not the player’s learned-recipe record.

sections.title: Item instance
paragraphs: One owned item identity/quantity and mutable properties, distinct from the shared item definition.

sections.title: GAS
paragraphs: Gameplay Ability System: attributes, abilities, effects and associated execution/prediction mechanisms, not MMO persistence.

sections.title: Gameplay Tag
paragraphs: A named vocabulary entry used in definitions/rules, not a permission bypass.

sections.title: Flipbook
paragraphs: A Paper2D sequence of sprite frames and durations.

sections.title: TileSet / TileMap
paragraphs: An atlas-derived tile definition and an arrangement of tiles/layers. Walkability and collision still require setup.

sections.title: PaperZD
paragraphs: Third-party 2D animation tooling. Exact installed APIs and overlay synchronization require verification.

sections.title: UMG focus
paragraphs: Which UI control receives keyboard/controller actions. Opening a widget does not pause the multiplayer world.

sections.title: Transaction
paragraphs: An atomic change whose related deductions, grants and receipt either commit together or do not.

sections.title: Idempotency
paragraphs: Repeating the same semantic request identity returns its original outcome without repeating its effects.

sections.title: Receipt
paragraphs: Durable evidence of the accepted command and result, written atomically with that result.

sections.title: Domain uniqueness
paragraphs: A separate invariant such as one catch per CastId, even when a malicious client uses different request IDs.

sections.title: Session lease / epoch
paragraphs: Time-bounded authority for one server to act for a character; an increasing epoch rejects stale owners.

sections.title: Zone transfer
paragraphs: A coordinated change of authoritative gameplay server for one character, not a whole-server map change.

sections.title: Content migration
paragraphs: An explicit versioned mapping of stored IDs/values to a changed supported schema/catalog.

sections.title: Contribution meter
paragraphs: A view of committed project progress, not a counter that the widget may increment authoritatively.

sections.title: Accessibility alternative
paragraphs: An equivalent usable interaction mode, such as forgiving fishing timing, with the same server validation.

sections.title: Outbox
paragraphs: Durable delivery work saved with a transaction so committed changes can be projected after a crash.
