sections.title: Progression value ownership and defaults
paragraphs: Extend the existing Progression object, not a new manager, component, table owner or parallel save. VocationId remains the only authoritative active-vocation selector. Progression.Vocations is keyed by stable vocation ID; an entry’s identity is its key, never its position, display name or an additional mutable ID field. The active key must exist and every trained inactive entry survives.

Progression.Combat belongs to the permanent CombatDisciplineId. Each vocation value stores TotalXP, DefinitionVersion, MasteryXP, UnspentMasteryPoints, PurchasedSkillIds, PurchasedTalentIds, LearnedRecipeIds, UnlockedTechniqueIds and AccomplishmentIds. Integer values are nonnegative and bounded; ID collections are duplicate-free and validated against their versioned definitions. Mastery rank derives from MasteryXP and the authored mastery graph. Do not keep an independently writable saved Level or MasteryRank.

Combat and vocation levels derive independently from TotalXP and their pinned, validated LevelThresholds. No formula reads the other track’s level. ContentVersion on the definition is the stored DefinitionVersion; reject unavailable versions rather than silently using a changed curve. First training uses the vocation’s InitialXP (default 0), which must map to Level 1; initialize mastery XP/points to 0 and earned sets empty except explicitly authored initial recipes/unlocks. Entry creation and any permitted initial grants occur once under the existing transaction/domain-uniqueness rules.

Revision is the existing character aggregate revision and also the progression/build projection revision. Every committed XP award, purchase or active-vocation change advances it once; do not add a separately writable build/level counter. SchemaVersion versions serialization, not player progress. Preserve reputation, inventory records, quest outcomes and Living Regions contributions in their existing owners.

One-time award history remains governed by the existing durable domain outcomes and Record_CommandReceipt, not by cached ability handles. Threshold awards happen on validated XP deltas once; import, hydration, switching and permission reconstruction grant no XP, points, items or already-earned unlock rewards.

sections.title: Compatible migration and unresolved legacy identities
paragraphs: Schema 2 below is the proposed next documentation contract; no deployed schema or actual save fixtures were found in mmo_docs. Before rollout inventory real supported versions and codecs. Keep the old representation readable, back up originals and validate conversion into temporary values before an atomic revision/schema update. Do not treat this prose as an executed database migration.

For a supported single-vocation legacy record, retain VocationId and move its existing vocation XP/mastery/purchases/recipes/techniques/accomplishments into Progression.Vocations[VocationId]. Preserve the combat ledger, talents and unspent combat points separately, plus all unrelated fields and unique reward outcomes. After conversion only the new keyed value is authoritative; deprecated fields remain read-only compatibility input, never dual-written. Reapplying the migration to schema 2 is a no-op.

Preserve every existing historical vocation record by its original stable ID. If an old format did not store a particular fact, use documented empty/zero defaults only where absence is proven to mean never earned. Unknown or conflicting history is not proof of an untrained vocation: retain the raw record, quarantine conflicting writes and recover from trusted records/receipts/backups or explicit migration review. Do not silently reset or discard earned progression.

Backfill CombatDisciplineId or FactionId only from an unambiguous trusted original selection. Otherwise return MigrationNeedsIdentitySelection and do not admit gameplay. Resolve through an authenticated, audited one-time legacy completion using approved available definitions while the record is fenced; preserve existing XP/talents and require a reviewed mapping when they constrain compatibility. Commit the decision and receipt atomically, then apply the permanent lock. Never assign a default class, infer allegiance from reputation or expose repeated class changes.

A missing inactive key in a validated current-schema record means never trained. A missing active key, duplicate serialized key, negative/overflowed XP, unknown/removed definition, inconsistent purchased IDs or unsupported schema/definition version is a load/migration failure, not permission to initialize over old data. Reject/quarantine while retaining the original; do not fall back to a fresh character. A content migration preserves XP, earned points/purchases and one-time outcomes; recompute views without replaying threshold rewards.

sections.title: Future-game progression acceptance matrix
paragraphs: Every row is NOT RUN IN UNREAL. Automated repository checks validate source contracts and fixture expectations only. Record the real build/service/content versions, before/after aggregate values, request/receipt IDs, revisions, ability/modifier source counts and failure evidence when these procedures execute.

rows: For each approved faction, each of four available disciplines and each of five available vocations, create through the normal UI and inspect storage; gate nonintegrated choices instead of claiming they ran.
One immutable faction/class and one active vocation persist, with independent initial XP and one kit/name/receipt outcome. All 20 available class/vocation pairs are legal.
Remove CombatDisciplineId from the request and submit.
CombatDisciplineRequired; no character, name reservation, item or receipt claiming success.
Use unsupported and unavailable class/vocation IDs separately; omit or forge faction, then remove its approved catalog.
CombatDisciplineUnavailable / VocationUnavailable / FactionRequired / FactionUnavailable / IdentityCatalogUnavailable; unchanged state.
After creation, forge a class replacement through the client command and a generic service patch; repeat for faction. Exercise same-class talent respec separately.
PermanentIdentityLocked for identity changes, with no XP/talent loss; only existing within-class respec is allowed.
Seed Vanguard 35 / Forgekeeper 20; satisfy current trainer eligibility and switch to never-trained Hearthkeeper.
Vanguard remains 35 with identical XP/talents/class grants; Hearthkeeper starts at defined XP and Level 1, Forgekeeper’s complete record remains.
Train Hearthkeeper to 12; after satisfying existing eligibility return to Forgekeeper, then Hearthkeeper.
Restore Forgekeeper 20 and Hearthkeeper 12 with exact saved XP, mastery, points, skills, talents, recipes, techniques and accomplishments.
Repeat eligible switches and same-active requests; count unique item/mastery/unlock outcomes and source-specific grants.
No history loss, duplicated rewards or modifiers; AlreadyActive changes nothing. Existing fee, if authored, is charged once per genuinely committed change only.
Snapshot Progression.Combat, CombatDisciplineId, faction, combat grant sources, inventory item IDs, quests and region contributions around each switch.
All remain identical except a specifically authored retraining currency debit; vocation mastery points never spend as combat points.
After switching, send a stale exclusive ability activation and old specialist recipe command; also try basic fishing/general gathering.
InactiveVocationPermission rejects specialist use at authoritative acceptance/commit; learned data stays stored, general activities and class abilities remain available.
Logout, reconnect, respawn and transfer only one character between Thornmere/Elderwood; restart the owning process and inspect full snapshots.
All trained histories and permanent identities survive; one active vocation/lease, no repeated grants; remaining clients stay in their zones.
Drop the accepted change response; retry it unchanged on reconnect with a fresh lease. Switch again, then replay the earlier accepted request and try a changed target under that RequestId.
Original authorized receipt returned without mutation or fees; older receipt cannot overwrite newer active state. Changed payload returns RequestIdentityConflict.
Submit two eligible target changes with the same ExpectedRevisions; repeat from a fenced old zone.
One coherent commit plus one StaleRevision; stale epoch cannot write. Never two active vocations, two fees or a lost history.
Try an invalid trainer/range and switch with unresolved craft/trade/transfer/XP work. Inject failure before commit, after commit/before reply and before outbox delivery.
Reject before mutation or resolve PendingSave/RecoveryPending by receipt. An atomic original or new state survives; replayed publication rebuilds no rewards.
Use Combat 40 / Forgekeeper 5 and Combat 10 / Hearthkeeper 30. Award combat XP alone, vocation XP alone, then an explicitly dual-XP quest and replay its completion.
Each ledger changes only by its own authored amount; dual award commits once with the unique quest outcome; delayed XP is never redirected to another vocation.
Round-trip supported single-vocation and multi-vocation legacy snapshots, then rerun migration. Include missing class, missing active history, unknown IDs/versions, duplicate keys and negative XP.

Preserve all recoverable progress and outcomes with no grants replay. Unresolved identities require audited one-time completion; corrupt/ambiguous records are retained and quarantined, never reset or default-assigned.
Run the same path with one human first, then 2 clients and the existing 5/10/30 cases when available; use NPC/base-activity alternatives.
Identity/progression rules do not change with population; essential vocation progress and retraining never require another human.

pages.title: Four vertical-slice acceptance checkpoints
pages.summary: Each checkpoint must work from the normal player flow.

sections.title: Slice A · after Phase 10
paragraphs: Create or select a valid starting character, enter Thornmere, move with correct facing, transfer to Elderwood while another player stays, attack an enemy, receive combat XP and reconnect. Inventory loot is not claimed before Phase 11. Account/provider, plugin and art integrations must have real evidence.

sections.title: Slice B · after Phase 19, adjusted
paragraphs: Play Forgekeeper, Hearthkeeper and Wayfinder separately through their complete starter outings: mine/salvage/forge, fish/farm/bake and track/map/report. Early NPC supplies and the small durable project board make the solo route self-sufficient. The source’s Phase 18 checkpoint precedes cartography; ADR-002 corrects that dependency.

sections.title: Slice C · after Phase 26
paragraphs: All five vocations contribute through different activities. One human can complete the core repair/danger milestone; newcomers see current region state. Run 1/2/5/10/30 contention and parity cases where the actual environment supports them. Arithmetic simulation is not this acceptance test.

sections.title: Slice D · after Phase 31
paragraphs: Complete the six-region content route, solo/group dungeons, trade/social flows, all major UI and real deployment/recovery tests. Verify packaging, migrations, restore, bad-data/replay and performance. This manual currently supplies initial contracts, not a passing Slice D.
